Ecological Identity Where Have I Been This Semester

Nov 20, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

I can feel myself changing; I know I look at things differently than I did before. At the beginning of the semester, I was worried about how I would be able to fit environmental education into the Physics curriculum. Now, I feel like I have the whole weight of the world on my shoulders. I feel like I’m at a crossroads where not only do I need to be taking less from the environment, I need to start giving back. I’m feeling a little overwhelmed right now as to what I am to do next. —

Author: Ben.Harack

I know the feeling. I have hit that point a few times in my life. One of them I remember keenly. I was driving to Saskatoon for a badminton tournament. I think it was wintertime, late 2007. My head was full from reading Cradle to Cradle and from (for the first time) really confronting the multitude of issues that face the viability of our civilization. I remember keenly as I passed Craik that I thought a big thought. I thought of change, and of knowledge. At that moment I glimpsed a vision of human potential by comprehending a portion of my own. Out of this moment, the support of some friends, and our subsequent efforts, Vision of Earth was eventually born. My life has been utterly changed, and it has been changed for the better.
